card.title: Fold a sheet of paper 42 times

body.question: Assume a sheet of paper is 0.1 mm thick. If you could fold it in half 42 times, about how thick would the stack be, in kilometres?
body.reveal: About 440,000 km, which is farther than the Moon (roughly 380,000 km away). Each fold doubles the thickness, so 0.1 mm × 2^42 ≈ 440 million metres.

probes.question: Assume 0.1 mm paper. How thick, in km, would the stack be after 42 folds in half?

claims.claim: A sheet of paper is 0.1 mm thick
claims.note: Neither fetched page gives a paper thickness; Paper_folding page text had no relevant content. Consider rewording as an assumption ("Assume a sheet is 0.1 mm thick") or sourcing it.

claims.claim: 0.1 mm x 2^42 is about 440 million metres (439,804 km)
claims.note: Verified by calculation. 0.0001 m * 2^42 = 439,804,651 m = 439,805 km.
Fetched Moon page text says "averaging around 378,000 kilometers (235,000 mi)", not 384,400. Suggested wording: "farther than the Moon (about 380,000 km away)". 440,000 km exceeds either figure.

claims.claim: In real life you can't fold paper that many times
